minutes.headline: Commission approved after-the-fact deck at 899 Flat Hill Rd, let two dead trees at 54 Pine Acres be cut, and re-elected its chair.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission worked through a long hearing agenda, approving several notices of intent and continuing others to August 21 or September 4. The most debated item was an administrative determination on two dead trees at 54 Pine Acres, where the commission overrode the administrator's advice to keep one for habitat. It also approved Timber Rights and Hawes fund budgets, adopted next year's meeting dates, and re-chose the chair.

budget_items.what_was_said: The grant administrator said the three-quote requirement applies only to nonprofits, so town procurement processes govern. The commission authorised a representative to work on the engineering warrant.
A budget must be voted before accounting will allocate the funds. The proposal split the balance between professional services and supplies, partly to cover grant matching engineering fees.
The balance was split between professional services (contracting) and supplies. Part of the supplies money was already spent on a lawnmower.

budget_items.topic: Rent at the Hollis Road residence
budget_items.what_was_said: Raising rent to market rate was discussed but remains unresolved. The question of whether the trust terms allow it awaits a replacement town manager and advice from town counsel.

decisions.decision: Zero Courtland Circle hearing continued to August 21 because the applicant's engineer's paperwork was not submitted.
The 11:47 Mass hearing was not heard because of inadequate abutter notification and legal ad placement.
The administrator will ask town counsel to send another letter on the 45 Road 12 violation, with the commission wanting it closed within about 30 days and not wanting to fine.
For the 37 Fire Road emergency tree work, the owner is to file a retroactive administrative determination.
January meetings shifted to the 8th and 22nd. The administrator was asked to add normal-cadence July and August dates for next year.
The administrator was encouraged to inspect 390 Howard Street for erosion and runoff and keep a paper trail.

what_happened.line: The commission voted 3-1 to allow removal of both dead trees at 54 Pine Acres, a decision made in an administrative determination.
It approved three notices of intent for new construction on Cross Road lots, including a duplex, a single-family home and an addition with driveway.
It approved a field change at 899 Flat Hill Road as presented, 4-0.
Four hearings were continued to August 21 or September 4, one because an applicant's engineer's paperwork was not submitted.
It accepted the Timber Rights and Hawes fund budgets as proposed, adopted next year's meeting dates, and chose a chair again.

why_it_matters: Approvals on Cross Road and Flat Hill Road, and the continued hearings, decide what gets built near wetlands in town, and abutters can raise concerns at the continued hearings.
The two fund budgets set how conservation money is spent on professional services and supplies, including engineering fees tied to the Mass Trails grant.
watch_next: Continued hearings on August 21 (Courtland Circle, PJ Keating pump house, Arbor Street) and September 4 (390 Howard Street).
Town counsel's follow-up letter on the 45 Road 12 violation, which the commission wants closed within about 30 days.
